answer.answer: The six-hour observation eases the acute free-space condition but does not resolve or authorize the durable legacy-table retirement question. Compact replacements remain the active write path; legacy tables remain retained, non-writing storage.

claims.value: Recovered prior causal state: about 196 GiB was retained in legacy session tables. Earlier sampling showed writes flowing to compact replacement tables rather than legacy counterparts. The sharp free-space excursion was suspected to be transient MySQL work, but its precise cause remained unproven.

The new six-hour observation measured 68 GiB of filesystem free space, stable within 1 GiB; legacy session tables remained at zero writes per second while compact replacement tables continued receiving active writes. This indicates the emergency has eased, not that historical free-space capacity has been restored.

Legacy-table retirement and physical reclamation remain unauthorized. Zero observed writes supports the write-path cutover distinction, but does not substitute for replay, rollback, maintenance, and physical-reclaim approval.

Before proposing any destructive retirement operation: continue free-space and write-path monitoring; complete and accept replay/rehydration and rollback rehearsal evidence; obtain an approved schema-maintenance window; and separately approve the snapshot, runway, lock/runtime, rollback, and physical-reclamation plan.

answer.answer: Revised child checkpoint: use three occupied level-0 Base Cores, dedicating one core to each heavy machine. No two requested machines may share a core. Construction remains gated on confirming that existing and supporting heat keeps each core at or below 1,000.

claims.value: The prior durable architecture was an Update 1-only distributed backbone-and-spurs factory with protected core hubs, modular production cells, mining spurs, single-item rail lines and buffers, and rail upgrades driven by measured throughput rather than a monolithic mega-base.

The new requirement is one Constructorizer and two Facturers while every Base Core remains level 0. Their machine heat is 500 + 650 + 650 = 1,800 total. A level-0 core has 1,000 capacity, and exceeding it disables Fire Wave protection.

The safe revised layout uses at least three occupied level-0 cores: Core A hosts only the Constructorizer at 500 heat, leaving 500 capacity; Core B hosts only Facturer 1 at 650 heat, leaving 350; Core C hosts only Facturer 2 at 650 heat, leaving 350. Constructorizer plus Facturer is unsafe at 1,150, two Facturers are unsafe at 1,300, and all three are unsafe at 1,800, so every requested heavy machine must be isolated from the others. Existing and support-building heat must fit inside the stated remaining capacity at its respective core.

Before construction, inspect each intended core's live load and Update 1 unlocks, budget all required support heat, and proceed only where the projected total is no more than 1,000. Use only confirmed Update 1 equipment; do not rely on hidden or future content, disputed amplifier values, or pre-Update-1 guidance.

Required heavy-machine heat totals 1,800: Constructorizer 500, Facturer 1 650, and Facturer 2 650.
The revised design assigns the Constructorizer, Facturer 1, and Facturer 2 to three separate level-0 Base Cores.
Before other buildings are counted, the three cores respectively retain 500, 350, and 350 heat capacity.
No requested heavy machines have been asserted as already built or tested.
decisions: Reject every heavy-machine co-location: Constructorizer plus Facturer totals 1,150; two Facturers total 1,300; all three total 1,800. Each exceeds the 1,000 level-0 limit.
Use a minimum of three occupied level-0 cores: Core A for the Constructorizer only, Core B for Facturer 1 only, and Core C for Facturer 2 only.
Treat each core's remaining 500/350/350 capacity as a hard envelope for all existing load, power generation, extraction, processing, storage, and other heat-bearing support assigned to that core.
Preserve the distributed rail backbone, but use only confirmed Update 1 rail tiers and equipment. Do not depend on Rail v.4/v.5, hidden buildings, future recipes, or unverified amplifier cooling.
Do not begin construction until live core loads plus the complete planned support load have been measured and shown to remain at or below 1,000 on every occupied core.

Which required recipes and support machines are currently unlocked in the live Update 1 save?
Can zero-heat or sufficiently low-heat power sources supply 700 power to the Constructorizer and 850 power to each Facturer without breaching the per-core envelopes?
What measured input and output rates are required for the selected Constructorizer and Facturer recipes?
What capacity do Base Core Amplifiers actually provide in-game? Their descriptions and stored temperature fields conflict, so no amplifier benefit is included in the safety calculation.
next_actions: Select three candidate level-0 cores and record each live capacity/load reading and the heat of every existing building assigned to it.

Draft a per-core bill of buildings and heat: Core A must satisfy existing load + 500 Constructorizer heat + support heat <= 1,000; Cores B and C must each satisfy existing load + 650 Facturer heat + support heat <= 1,000.

Verify every planned machine, recipe, rail tier, storage building, and power source in the current Update 1 build menu; remove anything hidden, future-facing, unavailable, or known only from obsolete playtest guidance.
Only after all three budgets pass, construct and commission one isolated machine cell at a time, rechecking live core load and Fire Wave protection after each build.
Connect the validated cells through the existing backbone-and-spurs network, upgrading only confirmed Update 1 rail trunks when measured flow exceeds their current capacity.

claims.value: Straylight is a user-owned, portable agent context and durable-work layer that preserves learned knowledge and live resumable work state so later agents can inspect, revise, advance, and hand off complex work with source fidelity.

The result of roughly 1,070 mean estimated tokens for one-shot BM25 versus 2,932 for the prototype workspace showed that the process-per-operation prototype was less token-efficient on the narrow retrieval benchmark; it did not reject the workspace product or persistent API. Tokens rank below reasoning quality, the retrieval result remains a regression baseline, and the new gate requires separate reporting of cumulative cached replay and uncached input for the persistent implementation.

The first persistent build slice is a snapshot-pinned workspace service with typed, batchable open/refresh, query, read, and checkpoint-commit operations: reopen parent cp_de0046ff6008f7e71798 at revision rev_000001_5bb8d7cf1222; refresh to rev_000002_7323ec9a8a69 using its delta and expose the changed evidence; combine exact and lexical retrieval with a pluggable semantic path; preserve full source references; and commit an immutable child naming its parent without reconstructing the complete prior corpus.

The slice passes when each transition case completes in no more than four workspace calls, its answer claims match the direct-filesystem claims, refresh exposes the N-to-N+1 diff, the committed child is immutable and records its parent plus source references, cached replay and uncached input are reported separately, and the checkpoint-plus-delta path does not reconstruct the complete prior corpus.

claims.value: Straylight is a user-owned, portable, agent-first context and durable-work layer that preserves both learned knowledge and live resumable work state so later agents can inspect, revise, and advance complex work.

The completed retrieval result is only a regression baseline: its tuned score is not holdout evidence or product validation. Transition measurements must also report cumulative cached replay and uncached input separately.

The first persistent build slice is an end-to-end snapshot-pinned flow that reopens a revision-N parent, refreshes to N+1 with an evidence diff, performs typed batched exact and lexical retrieval through a pluggable semantic path, and commits an immutable child with parent and exact source references.

The transition passes when a case uses no more than four completed workspace calls, matches the direct-filesystem answer claims, avoids reconstructing the complete corpus when checkpoint plus delta suffice, preserves verifiable parent/source lineage, and reports cached replay separately from uncached input.

current_state: The owner-authorized N+1 delta moves Straylight from expanded evaluation into implementation.
The completed retrieval-readiness result covered too narrow a slice; Retrieval policy 0.2 is only a frozen regression baseline, and its tuned score is not holdout evidence.
The target is an agent-first durable-work layer preserving learned knowledge and live resumable state with provenance and full-source access.
Acceptance requires reopening the exact parent at N, exposing the N+1 source change, answering without full-corpus reconstruction, and persisting a child with verifiable lineage.
Acceptance requires no more than four workspace calls and claim parity with the direct-filesystem control.
Cached replay and uncached input tokens must be measured separately.
decisions: Build the reopen, refresh/diff, batched retrieval, and immutable child-commit flow as one persistent vertical slice.
Support exact and lexical retrieval through typed batched calls with a pluggable semantic-provider interface.
Keep the process-per-operation BM25 shell only as a regression fixture.
Do not treat the tuned retrieval score as holdout evidence or product validation.
